caseStudy.title: Bucherer
caseStudy.lead: A quick iOS proof of concept for a luxury watch retailer: can the existing online shop, partly built on Salesforce, run inside a native app, keep customers signed in and complete a purchase?

facts.label: Client
facts.value: Bucherer, luxury watch and jewellery retailer

brief.title: The brief
text: Before committing to an app, the retailer wanted to know how far the existing web shop could carry it. Some of the shop runs on Salesforce and some does not, so the flows had to be checked across both, from sign-in to checkout.
I worked with the agency managers and the web developers, and the result had to be an honest answer on what the shop can do inside a native app.

contributions.title: What I did
items: Built a SwiftUI prototype with a WKWebView wrapped in UIViewRepresentable.
Kept sessions across launches with persistent cookies in the default website data store.
Logged every navigation to trace how sign-in, cart and checkout move between the Salesforce and non-Salesforce parts.
Tried routing cart, checkout and payment pages to Safari as a fallback option.
Documented the issues and risks found along the way.

findings.title: What the PoC found
findings.text: The shop works inside the app, with a list of issues to fix on the web side and a few risks to plan for.

items.title: AVIF images blink while loading
items.text: Visible flicker inside the WebView, serious enough to risk an App Store rejection.

items.title: Session ends after 24 hours
items.text: Customers would be signed out daily unless the session handling changes.

items.title: Layout details in the WebView
items.text: Accessibility button position, cut images, back-to-top button and footer position.

items.title: Account flows on test systems
items.text: Password recovery on DEV, no registration mail on staging, tab selection in My Account.

items.title: Store payment rules
items.text: External payment is allowed for physical goods, which watches are, but it has to be planned with store review in mind.

items.title: Dependence on the web platform
items.text: An app built on the shop depends on the shop staying stable and on WebView limits.

team.title: Team
team.text: The only mobile engineer on the engagement, in contact with the agency managers and the web developers.

outcome.title: The result
outcome.text: A clear answer on what the web shop can and cannot do inside a native app, and the issues to fix before an app could launch.
